nodes.label: handoff.md
nodes.summary: Handoff doc briefing whoever builds a desktop GUI on top of the already-complete reel2movie pipeline; points to brainstorm.md (scope), flow.md (pipeline flow), and PROGRESS.md (full rationale) rather than duplicating them.

nodes.label: The real integration point for a GUI: don't shell out, import it
nodes.norm_label: the real integration point for a gui: don't shell out, import it
nodes.summary: The CLI (reel2movie/cli.py) is a thin wrapper around build_default_pipeline_deps() (reads env vars, wires real clients) and run_pipeline(reel_url, deps) -> PipelineResult. Says call run_pipeline from a background thread, not the GUI's main thread. If using a different language/runtime, treat reel2movie as an external process instead and read the Subprocess gotcha first.

nodes.label: Performance -- this is not a fast, synchronous call
nodes.norm_label: performance -- this is not a fast, synchronous call
nodes.summary: Real observed durations across 11 live reels: caption/comment-only hits 10-60 seconds; visual-fallback hits (dense 1fps sampling -> Pillow dedup -> one Claude CLI vision call per surviving unique frame) ranged ~50 seconds to ~24 minutes, driven by video length and how much the dedup pass collapses. Instructs: background thread/process, an indeterminate progress spinner (no cheap way to predict completion time), don't block the UI thread on run_pipeline().

nodes.label: Ambiguous titles can resolve inconsistently across repeated detections in the same reel
nodes.norm_label: ambiguous titles can resolve inconsistently across repeated detections in the same reel
nodes.rationale: A known, documented limitation (brainstorm.md's 'Known hard cases'), not a new bug -- the GUI will occasionally show what looks like the 'same' title twice with different years/posters; whoever builds the GUI must decide whether to surface that as-is or add client-side dedup-by-fuzzy-title-match.
nodes.summary: Dense sampling means the same on-screen text can be independently 'seen' in multiple frames; if the title itself is ambiguous (e.g. 'The Invitation' -- several real movies share that name), different frames' guesses can resolve to different TMDB entries in the same result set.

nodes.label: Sentiment isn't filtered
nodes.rationale: Explicitly an accepted v1 limitation per brainstorm.md, not something to silently 'fix' by adding filtering logic unless the user asks for it.
nodes.summary: A caption that mentions a movie only to say 'not as good as X' still surfaces X as a candidate.

nodes.label: Subprocess stdout gotcha (yt-dlp progress bar corrupts JSON parsing)
nodes.norm_label: subprocess stdout gotcha (yt-dlp progress bar corrupts json parsing)
nodes.rationale: Workaround used during testing: find the first `{` in captured stdout and parse from there rather than assuming pure JSON. A cleaner root-cause fix (adding noprogress: True to the opts dict in ytdlp_client.py) was identified but not applied -- flagged as a good first improvement for whoever picks this up since it fixes every caller, not just one GUI's parsing code.
nodes.summary: If shelling out to the CLI instead of importing the package: yt_dlp's download-progress meter writes directly to stdout even though ytdlp_client.py sets quiet: True (quiet silences yt-dlp's logger but not its progress-bar writer). Reproduced directly during live testing -- naive stdout capture + json.loads() failed because the progress line landed on the same line as the CLI's opening `{`.

nodes.label: Suggested desktop-app architecture (not prescriptive)
nodes.rationale: Trade-off is simplicity/type-safety (direct import) versus stack flexibility (subprocess), with the subprocess route inheriting the stdout-parsing gotcha as its cost. Either way: run the pipeline off the UI thread, show a progress/spinner state, render tmdb: null entries distinctly rather than hiding them.
nodes.summary: Two reasonable shapes: (1) Python GUI (Tkinter/PySide6/customtkinter) importing reel2movie directly -- simplest, typed objects, no subprocess/JSON-parsing layer, avoids the stdout gotcha; (2) any GUI stack with reel2movie as a subprocess -- more flexible stack choice, but owns stdout-parsing robustness and loses typed Recommendation/ResolvedMovie objects in favor of the raw JSON contract.

nodes.label: TMDB connection resets are routine, not rare
nodes.norm_label: tmdb connection resets are routine, not rare
nodes.rationale: The GUI should present unresolved recommendations gracefully (e.g. 'detected but couldn't verify on TMDB -- try again'), not treat tmdb: null as an extraction failure.
nodes.summary: tmdb/client.py already retries transient connection errors 3x with backoff, but in real testing some lookups still exhausted the retry budget and came back tmdb: null for perfectly real, correctly-detected titles (e.g. '27 Dresses', 'Failure to Launch' in one real test run).

nodes.label: The biggest desktop-app design constraint: the `claude` CLI dependency
nodes.norm_label: the biggest desktop-app design constraint: the `claude` cli dependency
nodes.rationale: Correct for this project's own dev/testing use but 'almost certainly wrong for anything you'd ship to another person's machine' -- they'd need the claude CLI installed and logged into their own subscription, not normal end-user desktop-app behavior. Must be decided explicitly: personal-machine tool keeps the default; anything shipped to someone else's machine should set VISION_BACKEND=anthropic_api and bundle/require a real ANTHROPIC_API_KEY instead, dropping the claude-CLI dependency entirely.
nodes.summary: By default (VISION_BACKEND=claude_code) both the visual-fallback detector and the text-extraction fallback shell out to a locally-installed `claude` CLI binary authenticated against a Claude Pro/Max subscription -- not pip-installable, not bundled.

nodes.norm_label: output contract (if going through the cli/subprocess route)
nodes.summary: Documents the exact stdout JSON shape of `python3 -m reel2movie <url>` (reel_url, recommendations[].query/source/confidence/tmdb). tmdb is null when a candidate was detected but failed to resolve against TMDB -- the GUI must handle this, it happens routinely, not just on malformed input. poster_path is a TMDB-relative path; full image URL is https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/w500<poster_path>, not currently built anywhere in this codebase.

nodes.rationale: Final GUI subtask: wires Subtask 1's background engine (gui/workers.py) to Subtask 2's presentational widgets (gui/widgets.py) into one runnable MainWindow app, adds the gui/main.py entry point and gui/styles.qss styling, and declares PySide6 as the 'gui' optional-dependency group in pyproject.toml. A high-effort code-review pass found two real bugs — Enter-key re-entrancy and close-mid-run thread destruction — both fixed in this pass — plus one blocking cross-module copy bug in ApiKeyPromptPanel (TMDB-labeled copy shown on what is actually the Anthropic-key fallback panel), which was reported but left out of scope for a follow-up pass. Independent re-verification (empty-URL validation, missing-TMDB_API_KEY error path, double-Run-click/Enter-bypass state reset) confirmed the fixes; full test suite (262 passed) showed no regression in reel2movie/.

nodes.label: ApiKeyPromptPanel copy-mismatch bug and its fix
nodes.norm_label: apikeypromptpanel copy-mismatch bug and its fix
nodes.rationale: The panel's title, explanation, and placeholder text all described TMDB verification and a TMDB key, while the code path that shows it stores the entered value as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for the vision-backend fallback — a pure copy-mismatch (no logic/signal/signature change needed), closed by rewriting the three strings to describe the Anthropic-key/claude-CLI-fallback context instead; this was originally flagged as GUI Subtask 3's review finding #2.

nodes.label: GUI follow-up: fixed ApiKeyPromptPanel's mismatched copy
nodes.norm_label: gui follow-up: fixed apikeypromptpanel's mismatched copy
nodes.rationale: ApiKeyPromptPanel's hardcoded copy said 'TMDB API Key Needed' and described verifying titles against TMDB, but main_window.py only ever shows the panel on the claude-CLI-unusable → Anthropic-key fallback path and stores the submitted value as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, never TMDB_API_KEY — so a user following the on-screen instructions would paste a TMDB key that gets stored under the wrong variable, leaving TMDB_API_KEY still unset and producing an unrelated-looking top-level error with no path forward. Fixed by changing the title to 'Anthropic API Key Needed', rewording the explanation to describe the actual claude-CLI-unavailable/vision-fallback context, and updating the QLineEdit placeholder ('Paste your TMDB API key' → 'Paste your Anthropic API key') to match. Scope: pure string-content change only — key_submitted signal, constructor signature, and other classes in the file untouched; verified via ast.parse, a smoke test of key_submitted firing correctly, and the full test suite (262 passed).

nodes.label: Real bug fixed: close-mid-run thread destruction
nodes.norm_label: real bug fixed: close-mid-run thread destruction
nodes.rationale: Neither QThread worker (ClaudeCliCheckWorker, PipelineRunner) was Qt-parented to MainWindow (both constructed with parent=None), so closing the window mid-run didn't stop them, and process teardown while a worker was still executing risked the same 'destroyed while running' crash. Fixed with a minimal closeEvent override: ignore the close while either worker isRunning(), otherwise proceed normally.

nodes.label: Real bug fixed: Enter-key re-entrancy in _on_run_clicked
nodes.norm_label: real bug fixed: enter-key re-entrancy in _on_run_clicked
nodes.rationale: _on_run_clicked had no re-entrancy guard, and url_input.returnPressed fires regardless of run_button's disabled state, so pressing Enter while a CLI check or pipeline run was already in flight started a second ClaudeCliCheckWorker/PipelineRunner and overwrote the still-running one's worker reference — risking Qt's 'QThread: Destroyed while thread is still running' and racing succeeded/failed signals. Fixed with a one-line guard at the top of _on_run_clicked (if not self.run_button.isEnabled(): return), since run_button's enabled state already tracks precisely whether a background op is in flight.

nodes.rationale: TMDBHttpClient.search_movie() was intermittently failing with requests.exceptions.ConnectionError (TLS handshake resets) during live end-to-end testing, so hand-rolled retry-with-backoff (3 attempts, 0.5s then 1.0s sleeps) was added around the network call rather than adding a tenacity or urllib3 Retry dependency, since a single call site made exact backoff-value/exception-type control simpler to express directly.

hyperedges.label: Prioritized signal-source waterfall (caption > creator comment > frame sampling)
VISION_BACKEND selection mechanism (decision -> implementation -> GUI consequence)
hyperedges.summary: A single design decision (default to a local claude-CLI subscription instead of a metered Anthropic API key for visual detection) originates in vast-wobbling-owl.md's plan being revised, is implemented via config.get_vision_backend()/build_default_pipeline_deps() in the claude_code_cli_vision_backend follow-up, is flagged in handoff.md as a desktop-distribution constraint the GUI builder must decide on explicitly, and is operationalized at runtime by gui/workers.py's CLI-usability check + anthropic_api fallback — no single pairwise edge captures that all four are the same decision thread.
